newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian govt paper prices down, o/night credits up.
newsitem.headline: Russian govt paper prices down, o/night credits up.

text.p: Prices of Russian long-term government paper slipped in quiet trading as banks started selling after receiving accruals from the week-end, dealers said.
Overnight rouble credits edged up on expectations of a rouble shortage.
*Average yield rose to 18.6 pct from 17.9 pct on Friday
*Turnover fell to 2.75 trln rbls from 3.35 trln rbls
*Banks transferred 2.20 trln rbls for trading
*Central bank sold 297 bln rbls of T-bills
rouble/dollar July 28 July 25
midday morning close
tomorrow settlement 5,801-02 5,800-01 5,799-800
overnight credits (%) 3-8 8-15 1-5

"At the start of trading prices of short-term GKO Treasury bills slipped as the market was not sure what will happen on the overnight credits market," said Aljba-Alliance Bank dealer Mikhail Vasilyev.
"But later T-bill prices rose, while OFZ bonds, where banks hold big speculative positions, edged down, as banks got their weekend accruals and started selling."
Yields of long-term goverment paper closed at 18.8-18.9 percent after 18.7 percent in the middle of the trading.
Vasilyev said the market was waiting for funds from last week's auction of telecoms holding Svyazinvest to return.
The losing consortium, which deposited $400 million for Friday's auction, will get its money back within three banking days.
"It is likely that the money will make it to (Wednesday's) auctions," Vasilyev said. "Many banks are betting on this and holding paper."
On the foreign exchange market, expectations of a rouble shortage pushed overnight credit rates to 15 percent, making swap operations profitable, dealers said.
But the expectations turned out to be groundless and rates for tomorrow and today deliveries became equal, they said.
However, credit rates remained higher compared to Friday's close.
"In the morning we expected there will be no roubles and below an overnight rate of 15 percent it was profitable to make swaps," said Bank Menatep dealer Mikhail Zaretsky.
"Later it became obvious that interest in the rouble is weakening and levels became equal."
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
